text:
COP rose 0.84% today to $136.12, recovering modestly from a sharp drop two days earlier when the stock fell nearly $5. The bounce appears tied to a combination of geopolitical tension in the Middle East—with reports of Iranian-backed drone and projectile attacks on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain—which typically supports oil prices, and broader energy demand signals from the IEA warning that data center electricity use could double by 2030, adding structural pressure on global energy supply. Oil prices remain elevated at nearly $90 per barrel domestically and $93 globally, providing a steady backdrop for an oil major's earnings.

The stock had fallen sharply from $142 just a week ago, so today's gain reads as a partial stabilization rather than a fresh breakout. Geopolitical risk premiums in oil markets can be fleeting, but the longer-term demand story—from AI data centers, constrained European gas supplies heading into winter, and potential U.S. interest rate shifts—continues to undergird energy valuations.
